abstract: Clustering is the standard route from a molecular dynamics trajectory to a small set of interpretable conformational states, yet it is usually performed outside the molecular viewer, leaving cluster assignments to be exported, tracked, and mapped back onto the structures by hand. We present VMDance, an open-source plugin that brings the MDANCE family of $n$-ary similarity clustering methods into VMD. Through a graphical interface backed by a C++ implementation, it provides \kmeans{} NANI, HELM, eQual, and DIVINE clustering, together with PRIME representative-structure selection. These methods scale linearly with the number of frames and support deterministic initialization, so partitions can be reproduced exactly and recomputed interactively. Cluster assignments, quality metrics, and representative structures are linked to the loaded trajectory, keeping the analysis of conformational states alongside the structures themselves. VMDance is freely available at \url{https://github.com/diegoenry/vmd-mdance-plugin}
